content.text: The Mistake Almost Every Creator Makes First

This trap is set when creators rely on conventional payment processors like Stripe, PayPal, and Gumroad, which often restrict or ban users from certain countries, leaving them unable to collect payments or even access their own accounts. In the case of Nigeria, for instance, PayPal's restrictions on the country have left many creators unable to sell digital products to international buyers, including those in the US, Europe, or Asia.
Why This Keeps Happening Even to Experienced Sellers

Experienced sellers often underestimate the risks of relying on third-party infrastructure, assuming that their own business is too small or too niche to be affected. However, the reality is that even large and established businesses can suffer from infrastructure restrictions, which can bring their entire operation to a grinding halt. In Pakistan, for example, the government has imposed restrictions on online payments, making it difficult for creators to receive payments for their digital products.
The Real Cost of Getting This Wrong

When creators rely on third-party infrastructure that can be shut down or restricted at any moment, they risk losing their entire business overnight. This can lead to financial ruin, damage to their reputation, and even emotional distress. In addition, they may also face penalties and fines for non-compliance with local regulations. In Ghana, for instance, creators who sell digital products without proper licensing and registration may face fines of up to $10,000.
Don't let infrastructure restrictions hold you back from selling digital products internationally.
How to Build the Stack That Cannot Be Taken Down

The solution to this problem is to build a sovereign digital commerce stack that is completely independent of third-party infrastructure. This means using free and open-source tools like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, and Supabase to host and manage digital products, as well as using blockchain-based payment processors like NOWPayments to accept payments from international buyers. By doing so, creators can ensure that their business remains operational even if their third-party infrastructure is shut down or restricted.
